reference_answer:
Use the inherited rational-entry backend for the initial matrix: x,y∈Q, regarded as real numbers. For D=[[x,y],[y,-x]], the two row self-overlaps are x²+y² and y²+(-x)²=x²+y². The cross-overlaps are xy+y(-x)=0 and yx+(-x)y=0. Consequently DD^T=(x²+y²)I2, and D is orthogonal exactly when x²+y²=1; the same equation gives D^T D=I2. These identities are polynomial algebra valid overQ andR. Automatic zero cross-overlap alone is not unit normalization.

The question separately asks whether a REAL y exists. For a fixed rational x viewed inR (indeed for any real x under this scalar extension), a real y with y²=1-x² exists iff|x|≤1. Necessity is y²≥0; sufficiency is y=±sqrt(1-x²). This is real-existence mathematics, not a claim that those witnesses have rational entries. Remaining within the inherited rational matrix backend, a rational y exists exactly when1-x² is a square of a rational number. For rational x=1/2 the required y=±sqrt(3)/2 is irrational: if sqrt3=a/b in lowest positive integer terms, a²=3b² forces3 to divide a and then b, a contradiction. Thus|x|≤1 alone is not a rational-completion theorem. Conversely x=3/5,y=4/5 is rational; x0 admits y±1. At x=1 or-1, y0 works over both carriers, so the largest possible |x| is1 in either carrier, although the interior rational-existence criterion is stricter.

The normalizer-one obstruction is independent of auxiliary dimension. Let J be any clean isometric embedding, J†J=I, and U any unitary (real orthogonal in the real case). Then ||J†UJ z||≤||UJz||=||z||. Hence every clean compression is a contraction. In particular a scalar c with|c|>1 cannot appear as a normalizer-one clean block in ANY signal-register dimension. More signal qubits do not remedy this. This also follows entrywise because an entry of a unit vector has magnitude≤1.

With conventional positive normalizer alpha and exact target A=alpha B, it is B=J†UJ=A/alpha that must have norm≤1; for a scalar c this requires alpha≥|c|. Raising alpha is the necessary normalization remedy, not enlarging the signal space at fixed alpha1. Over real matrices, a2x2 dilation then realizes c/alpha; over rational entries its rational completion condition still applies and no arbitrary real square-root witness is silently imported. The Gram lemmas prove conditional algebraic identities, not a general rational-existence, finite-bit synthesis, success-probability or efficient circuit theorem.
